title: Full of Mitzvos Like a Pomegranate
summary: One who counts money from a woman's hand to look at her will not escape Gehinnom, and whether Manoach, who "went after his wife," was an am ha'aretz. Better to walk behind a lion than behind a woman. Then Adam's 130 years of teshuvah apart from Chava, the dove's olive branch, "let my food be bitter but from Hashem's hand," song in a house at night, and why the fire of Gehinnom cannot touch Jewish sinners, who are full of mitzvos like a pomegranate.
key_ideas: Guard your eyes; even a great person can be drawn in.
Teshuvah means building fences so you don't fall back.
Better a bitter livelihood straight from Hashem than a sweet one from people.
Even the emptiest Jew is full of mitzvos like a pomegranate.
